rounds.proof_sketch: With batch_size=128 and BLOCK_SIZE=256: threads 128-255 skip accumulation (tid >= batch_size), so shared_sum[128-255] = 0.0f always. First reduction (stride=128) reads only from indices 128-255. Internal __syncthreads() after stride=128 ensures all threads 0-127 complete their accumulation before stride=64 reads from indices 64-127.
rounds.survival_reason: The removed __syncthreads() is structurally redundant for this specific configuration. Threads 128-255 never enter the accumulation loop since tid >= batch_size=128, so their shared_sum values remain at 0.0f from initialization. The first reduction iteration (stride=128) has threads 0-127 reading from shared_sum[128-255], which contain only these pre-initialized zeros. The __syncthreads() that remains inside the reduction loop ensures that before stride=64 begins, all threads have completed stride=128, which requires them to have finished their accumulation. No value pattern can change this structural property.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed-shape contract. Killing would require batch_size > 256 so that threads 128-255 participate in accumulation, creating a race between their writes and the reduction reads. With batch_size=128, threads 128-255 never enter the accumulation loop, making the sync before reduction unnecessary.
rounds.recommendations: When testing sync_remove mutations, identify whether the synchronization is structurally necessary for the specific launch configuration. A sync may be 'defensive' (needed only for larger configurations) vs 'essential' (needed for all valid configurations). Configuration-stress testing with batch_size > BLOCK_SIZE would have revealed this sync is only needed for larger batches.
